parts.text: In this experiment, you will determine the diameter of a marble by two methods and calculate the density of the material from which the marble is made. Method 1 Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 1.1. Fig. 1.1 (Apparatus viewed from above)

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) Place the metre ruler on the bench with its scale facing upwards. Arrange one of the wooden blocks and the five marbles as shown in Fig. 1.1. Measure the length D for the five marbles. D = .......................................................... cm Using your value of D , calculate the average diameter d 1 of one marble. d 1 = .......................................................... cm [2]

ms.label: 1(a)(i)
ms.text:
sensible value for D (5.0–10.0 cm) and recorded to 1 or 2 d.p.
d1 = D / 5

ms.label: 1(a)(ii)
ms.text: effect of uncertainties reduced / diameters of marbles may vary

ms.label: 1(b)
ms.text:
use marble between two blocks and measure gap
d1 recorded and suitable means of ensuring accuracy e.g.:
measure gap in at least two places and check equal to ensure blocks are parallel / rotate marble to different axis and take
average of measurements

parts.label: i
parts.text: (c) (i) Use the top-pan balance as shown in Fig. 1.2 to measure the mass m of one of the marbles. Fig. 1.2 m = ....................................................... g [1]

ms.label: 1(c)(i)
ms.text: sensible value for m and recorded to at least 1 decimal place

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Pour approximately 25 cm 3 of water into the measuring cylinder. Record the reading V 1 of the water level in the measuring cylinder. V 1 = ........................................................ cm 3 Carefully place the 5 marbles into the water in the measuring cylinder as shown in Fig. 1.3. Fig. 1.3 Record the new reading V 2 of the water level in the measuring cylinder. V 2 = ........................................................ cm 3 Calculate a value for the average volume V of one marble. Use the equation V = V 2 – V 1 5 . V = ........................................................ cm 3 [1]

ms.label: 1(c)(ii)
ms.text: V2 > V1 and V calculated correctly

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Draw, on Fig. 1.3, an arrow showing the correct line of sight for reading the water level in the measuring cylinder. [1]

ms.label: 1(c)(iii)
ms.text: perpendicular arrow / line indicating lower meniscus

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) Calculate a value for the density ρ of the material from which the marble is made. Use your values of m from (c)(i) , V from (c)(ii) and the equation ρ = m V . ρ = .............................................. g / cm 3 [1]

ms.label: 1(c)(iv)
ms.text: ρ in sensible range recorded to 2 / 3 sig figs

ms.label: 1(d)
ms.text:
suitable source of inaccuracy e.g.:
graduations on measuring cylinder too large /
marbles may have different masses
improvement matching source of inaccuracy e.g.:
use smaller measuring cylinder or greater number of marbles /
measure 5 and take average mass
